question: Upstream #13169 reports a turn whose only delivered content is reasoning and whose `turn/end` still says `completed`. This machine had produced 0 of them, so nothing could say whether it happens here. Does a local endpoint that streams one reasoning block and a normal stop reproduce the shape, and does the scanner count it?

probe.homes: .tmp/r57-runs/reasoning and .tmp/r57-runs/text (isolated DSH_HOME; nothing under ~/.dsh is written)
probe.endpoint: .tmp/r57-fake-openai.mjs — `reasoning-only` streams two `reasoning_content` deltas then `finish_reason: "stop"`; `text` streams one content delta then `stop`
probe.why_the_shape_survives: the adapter's empty-response guard counts blocks, not usable content (`dsh-llm-pi-ai` `mapStopReason`: `if (message.content.length === 0)`), so one reasoning block passes and the loop ends the turn as `completed`
probe.note: the endpoint is local and synthetic: it reproduces the adapter shape, not a relay incident

findings: A turn that delivered only reasoning ends `completed` on this host, exactly as upstream #13169 describes, and the endpoint delivered it as a normal `stop` — so the shape is not a truncation and not an error.
The control run, same endpoint and same prompt with a text delta, ends the same way; the only difference a reader can see is the block type in the transcript.
The scanner counts the reasoning run and not the control, which is the rule P-0047 added; the completion census itself stays two.
not_proven: The endpoint is local and synthetic. It reproduces the adapter output, not a relay incident.
One route, one model, one prompt, one step per turn; a multi-step turn was not exercised.
The desktop app was not driven for this probe: both runs are headless CLI runs on the same host.
